Maladaptive Strategies.value: control eating strictly to feel in control
I imagine getting revenge on the people responsible
go along with whatever others want to feel safe

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it
Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel isolated and set apart from others
I feel permanently humiliated by what happened
Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation

vignette: Arjun was forty-one when he finally sat across from a clinician, his hands resting heavily on his knees as he described the morning he decided he could no longer manage alone. Three years earlier, during a routine supply run in a neighboring country, he had been seized by armed men who held him in a damp, windowless room for forty days. They were dressed in mismatched military fatigues, their authority absolute, their expectations rigid. He survived by shrinking into himself, swallowing his voice, and letting his body go numb so the humiliation of being reduced to an object would not break him. He had come to believe that surrender was the only path through the dark, a conviction that would shape every breath he took after his rescue. Returning to work as a park ranger had not offered him sanctuary. During a routine perimeter inspection, Arjun encountered a state wildlife enforcement officer directing traffic with a stern, clipped command from the edge of the trail. The officer’s dark uniform, the crisp cut of the hat, and the authoritative stance immediately conjured the fragmented snapshots of his captivity: the exact angle of a guard’s boot, the stark glare of a flashlight, the sudden, blinding flash of a door slamming shut. Each image arrived without warning, accompanied by a sharp, familiar ache across his ribs and forearms where the ropes had bit into him. The triggers had not just sparked a memory; they had weaponized his past, forcing the old humiliation forward. Arjun found himself convinced he had been fundamentally broken by what he endured, that any man with more strength would have refused to kneel. This self-recrimination, in turn, kept him locked in a state of defensive scanning, his eyes constantly tracking the posture of strangers and the cut of their clothes, which only ensured that the sight of authority figures continued to provoke him. His belief that he was permanently failed himself bled into the recollection itself, stripping the events of any emotional context and leaving only cold, disjointed frames. The mental fragments did not stay dormant. Once the snapshots took hold, they bled into full visceral intrusions, Arjun suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again. The memory directly triggered a constant, low-grade alarm; his body braced for violence, making even a sudden rustle of leaves or a companion stepping out from behind a tree cause him to flinch as if danger were closing in. Because the flashbacks felt so real, he stopped trusting reassurances from anyone, including his partner, who would remind him he was home and secure. The memory itself reinforced his conviction that he was permanently humiliated by what he endured, leaving him certain he would never recover. To cope with the mounting terror, he adopted rigid coping habits. His conviction that he was fundamentally weak drove him toward these coping mechanisms, convincing him that strict control and submission were the only ways to survive. Confronted with the weight of those returning moments, he began restricting his food intake, measuring every bite and chewing slowly to impose a strict order over his body, while silently replaying elaborate scenarios of vengeance against the men who had held him. During dispatch briefings at the ranger station, he also found himself yielding to every suggestion from the station chief, going along with whatever others wanted to feel safe. The fragments themselves heightened his alertness to danger, making him more sensitive to military discussions or uniformed patrols, which then pulled the next memory forward. His habitual people pleasing only deepened his self-recrimination, reinforcing the belief that someone else would not have gotten into this situation and would never have submitted. Over time, this rigid restriction and constant submission dulled his emotional processing, causing him to recall the captivity with complete numbness, as if it happened to a stranger. His internalized tension and suppressed anger made him hyper-reactive to any sign of authority, ensuring that encounters with uniformed personnel continued to spike his physiological alarms. The exhausting cycle of control and compliance left his nervous system permanently hypervigilant, preventing him from ever fully relaxing or trusting that he was safe. The relentless physiological arousal also fractured his recall, making the memories return as disjointed flashes rather than a coherent narrative. The unyielding alarm in his body confirmed his worst fears, convincing him that he was permanently damaged and isolated from normal life. His decision to seek help came when the numbness bled into his relationship with his partner, leaving him unable to share a quiet meal without checking the exits. He came to the clinic hoping to quiet the internal loop, though he was terrified that facing the memories would unravel him completely.
